## Illustrative dry-run cost, both ways

INPUTS ARE ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT MEASURED: 2,000,000 training tokens (2 epochs -> 4,000,000), 1200
tokens/s, 400,000 evaluation tokens, 1.2x restarts, 15 minutes billed setup. Only the rates and
their dates are fetched facts; the token count and throughput are placeholders until the dry run
is executed on the rented host.

| route | rate | billed work | compute | total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rented GPU (RunPod RTX A5000, fetched 2026-10-08) | $0.27/h | 1.5 GPU-hours (0.9 train + 0.1 eval + 0.3 setup) | $0.40 | $0.40 |
| managed per token (Fireworks up to 16B parameters (LoRA SFT), fetched 2026-10-08) | $0.50/1M tokens | 4.0M tokens | $2.40 | $2.40 |

Cheaper on these inputs: **rented GPU**. The
deciding inputs are the total training tokens, the measured tokens per second, and the billed
setup time per attempt: a short job on a rented card spends more time provisioning than training,
and a slow card can cost more than paying per token.

## What the dry run must record

Scope: 10-20 briefs from the training corpus, the same ones across arms.

- peak allocated and peak reserved VRAM (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated / max_memory_reserved)
- training tokens per second, and examples per second, at the pinned batch/sequence length
- examples per hour for generation, and acceptance yield per 20 examples
- GPU model, VRAM, provider, region, billing unit, and the quote_id from docs/eval/quotes.jsonl
- wall-clock per phase (setup, training, evaluation) and every restart that was billed
- storage GB-month and egress GB actually consumed

These measurements replace: estimateVram.total_gb, measured.tokensPerSecond, measured.evaluationTokensPerSecond, acceptance yield.

> These VMs have no GPU and, by owner decision, do not run models: this protocol is executed on the rented host and its output is copied back as a record, not run here.
